job.title: Product Operations Specialist @ Envoy global (TS, IN)
job.description:
Envoy Global is a proven innovator in the global immigration space. Our mission combines our industry-leading tech platform with holistic service to streamline, simplify and expedite the immigration process for employers and individuals.

We are looking for a **Product Operations Specialist** to anchor our Hyderabad product organization and serve as the operating backbone of the product PMO. You will work directly with the VP, Platform and Product Operations to align product, engineering, QA, design, documentation, and customer-facing teams around a common cadence, a common set of metrics, and a common way of working.

This role is about making the product organization run well: clear priorities, reliable data, predictable delivery, and decisions made on facts rather than anecdotes. You will define how product data is captured, make sure the right KPIs reach the right people, and remove the friction that slows teams down.

**As our Product Operations Specialist, you will be required to:**

**Cross-Team Alignment**
------------------------

* Act as the day-to-day connection point between product and platform leadership and the Hyderabad engineering, QA, design, UX, and support teams, and as the counterpart to product leadership in other geographies.
* Run the operating cadence: quarterly planning, monthly business reviews, sprint and release syncs, and weekly status check-ins. Own the agendas, pre-reads, decisions, and follow-ups.
* Identify cross-team dependencies and conflicts early, escalate with context, and track them to resolution.
* Translate roadmap priorities into clear, consistent messaging so every team understands what is changing, why, and what is expected of them.

**KPI Definition and Communication**
------------------------------------

* Partner with product leadership to define and maintain the KPI framework for the product organization, covering delivery, quality, adoption, customer health, and team productivity.
* Publish scorecards and dashboards on a regular schedule, with commentary on trends, risks, and variances rather than raw numbers alone.
* Brief product managers, engineering leads, and senior leadership on what the metrics mean and what actions they point to.
* Maintain a single, documented definition for every KPI (formula, source, owner, refresh frequency) so teams stop debating the numbers.

**Data Collection and Decision Support**
----------------------------------------

* Design and implement lightweight, repeatable processes for collecting product data from tools such as Jira, Confluence, the CRM, support platforms, product analytics, and customer feedback channels.
* Build and maintain dashboards and reports in the BI tools in use (for example Power BI, Tableau, or Looker) and keep underlying data clean and trustworthy.
* Establish data hygiene standards for work items, roadmap entries, and release records, and coach teams to follow them.
* Analyze trends in delivery, quality, adoption, and customer feedback, and turn them into recommendations for prioritization and investment.

**Product PMO Responsibilities**
--------------------------------

* **Portfolio tracking.** Own the product portfolio view: a single source of truth for initiatives, status, owners, timelines, dependencies, and health.
* **Roadmap governance.** Maintain the roadmap repository and coordinate roadmap reviews, ensuring changes are captured, communicated, and traceable.
* **Release and launch coordination.** Coordinate release calendars, go-live readiness checklists, and launch communications with engineering, QA, support, and go-to-market teams.
* **Risk and issue management.** Maintain a RAID log (risks, assumptions, issues, dependencies) across programs, drive mitigation owners, and surface top risks to leadership.
* **Resource and capacity planning.** Track capacity and allocation across product and engineering teams, and flag overcommitment or skill gaps ahead of planning cycles.
* **Budget and spend tracking.** Monitor budgets, vendor and contractor spend, and tool licenses for the product organization, and support forecasting.
* **Process and standards.** Define and document standard product processes, including intake and prioritization, PRD and spec templates, definition of ready and done, release management, and change control. Run periodic reviews for adherence and improvement.
* **Knowledge management.** Maintain product documentation, playbooks, and onboarding materials so new team members become productive quickly.
* **Governance and compliance support.** Support audit, compliance, and security reviews by keeping evidence of product processes, approvals, and release controls organized and current.
* Manage the product tooling stack (such as Jira, Confluence, roadmap and feedback tools): configuration, workflows, access, and user enablement, working with IT and tool administrators.

**AI-DLC Enablement: Tooling, Process, and Metrics**
----------------------------------------------------

Engineering and product teams run AI-DLC. This role defines how the environment, tools, and processes must be set up so AI-DLC-led development works, and defines how its results are measured.

* **Tool configuration.** Define the target configuration of the toolchain that supports AI-DLC, including AI development assistants and agents, work and planning tools (such as Jira and Confluence), source repositories, CI/CD, and test tooling. Specify the workflows, fields, templates, permissions, and integrations needed, and partner with IT, engineering, and tool administrators to implement them.
* **Work model in tools.** Define how Intents, Units of work, and Bolts are represented and linked in the tooling, replacing sprint and epic constructs where needed, so work is traceable from Intent through deployment.
* **Process and mechanisms.** Establish the processes and mechanisms for AI-DLC to run consistently: how Inception and Construction work is initiated, how Mob Elaboration and Mob Construction outputs are captured, where the persistent artifacts (plans, requirements, domain models, design documents) are stored, and how they are versioned and kept current.
* **Governance and controls.** Define the human validation checkpoints in each phase, who approves, and what evidence is retained, in coordination with security, compliance, and engineering leadership.
* **Metrics ownership.** Define the AI-DLC metrics framework: which metrics to track, how each is calculated, its data source and owner, and the targets. Examples include Bolt cycle time, Intent-to-release lead time, validation turnaround, rework and defect escape rates, AI-assisted contribution, cost, and team experience. Set pre-AI-DLC baselines.
* **Measurement and reporting.** Build the data collection mechanisms and dashboards that produce these metrics from the toolchain, and report results and trends to leadership with recommendations.
* **Standards and playbooks.** Document the standards, playbooks, and templates teams follow, including the organization-specific coding, design, and security standards the AI applies, and update them based on results.
* **Continuous tuning.** Use the metrics to recommend changes to tooling, process, and practice, and assess pilots to advise where to scale, adjust, or stop.

**Continuous Improvement**
